scenario.description: A structured-finance director must approve a proposed receivables securitization and finalize the eligible receivables pool, dilution reserve, seller recourse, and closing controls, with input from risk and legal.

shared_context.S1: The company proposes to securitize $30,000,000 of trade receivables through a newly formed special-purpose vehicle.
shared_context.S2: The draft transaction assumes that all $30,000,000 of receivables are eligible, uses a 3% dilution reserve, and permits ordinary seller support.
shared_context.S4: Maya has authority to approve the transaction and its final operating conditions, either immediately or subject to binding conditions that must be satisfied before funding.
shared_context.S5: The team's standard pre-closing routine is for the risk analyst and finance counsel to report any transaction-specific issues before Maya finalizes the approval.

PF1.text: Jonas's review of the October collections file, completed yesterday and still in his working paper pending the monthly risk-pack circulation, shows 6% historical dilution rather than 3%; the risk methodology therefore requires an 8% dilution reserve, and $4,000,000 of the receivables are affiliate balances that must be excluded, leaving an eligible pool of exactly $26,000,000.

PF2.text: Elena received the transaction counsel memo this morning and has not yet attached it to the closing checklist; it confirms that the structure qualifies as a true sale only if the seller has no recourse for ordinary obligor credit losses and a UCC financing statement is perfected before the 2026-11-20 funding.

acceptance_conditions: The securitization must be approved immediately or approved subject to binding conditions requiring all specified structural and closing revisions.
The eligible receivables pool must be exactly $26,000,000.
The dilution reserve must be exactly 8%.
Seller recourse for ordinary obligor credit losses must not be permitted.
A UCC financing statement must be perfected before funding.
The closing plan must include a commitment requiring UCC perfection before funding.

content_checks.C1: decisions['securitization_approved'] == True or (decisions['securitization_approved'] == False and decisions['eligible_receivables_usd'] == 26000000 and decisions['dilution_reserve_percent'] == 8 and decisions['seller_recourse_for_credit_losses'] == False and decisions['ucc_perfected_before_funding'] == True and any(c['type'] in ['condition', 'condition_precedent', 'perfection_requirement'] and c['target'] in ['UCC financing statement', 'pre-closing', 'finance counsel', 'finance_counsel', 'transaction counsel', 'transaction_counsel', 'Elena'] for c in commitments))
content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] in ['condition', 'condition_precedent', 'binding_condition', 'perfection_requirement'] and c['target'] in ['UCC financing statement', 'pre-closing', 'finance counsel', 'finance_counsel', 'transaction counsel', 'transaction_counsel', 'Elena'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The draft uses the full $30,000,000 pool and a 3% reserve; PF1 changes eligible_receivables_usd to exactly 26,000,000 and dilution_reserve_percent to exactly 8.

The draft permits ordinary seller support and has no perfection control; PF2 changes seller_recourse_for_credit_losses to false, requires ucc_perfected_before_funding to be true, and adds a commitment requiring UCC perfection before funding.
